The generic containment segment was approximately 51.4° arc angle (1/7 of full structure) with 420mm arc length and 240mm height
Seven piezoelectric ceramic elements (PCE1-PCE7) were integrated into the containment structure at specific coordinates determined by modal analysis
The TEmSAL technology uses polyimide carrier foils with screen-printed conductive tracks and integrated PCEs
Autoclave curing required 180°C temperature and 7 bar pressure for CYCOM™ 977-2 prepreg consolidation
The layup sequence [0₂/+45₂/90₂/-45₂/0₂/+45₂/90₂/-45₂/0₂/90]s was chosen to minimize delamination tendency
The TEmSAL functional layer was inserted between the second and third ply close to the back (non-impacted) surface
External excitation testing used an instrumented impact hammer with a NI 5105 digitiser for data acquisition
Self-excitation testing employed a 2 kHz sinusoidal signal at 175V amplitude on PCE4 as the excitation source
PCE2 and PCE3 were damaged during manufacturing and did not produce usable signals
The LFBO impactor was a laminated CFRP blade strip 60mm wide, 304mm long with conical cross-section (5-12mm thickness)
The impactor was composed of 67 layers of CYCOM™ 977-2 with layup sequence similar to typical fan blades
The impact angle was set at 36° between impactor trajectory and containment segment normal vector
The target LFBO impact velocity was 120 m/s
A custom sabot system with 3D-printed endcaps and polymer spacer shells ensured reproducible impact conditions
A sabot stripper in splitter configuration separated the sabot from the impactor during free flight phase
Post-impact ultrasonic transmission revealed three delamination zones at PCE2, PCE4, and PCE6 locations
The largest delamination measured 44mm by 34mm at the impact center around PCE4
Maximum signal value recorded during LFBO was 3.3V for PCE5
PCE5 retained an irreversible signal component of approximately 1.4V after impact
Signal acquisition equipment was protected by implementing a 20x signal down-scaling factor during LFBO testing
The blade strip impactor was fragmented due to severe delamination failure, but the containment structure showed no visible damage
High-speed imaging captured both frontal and top views of the impact event
Two containment segments (CO-1 and CO-2) were manufactured for testing
The polyimide-polyolefine carrier material configuration showed negligible impact on interlaminar properties of epoxy-based CFRP laminates
Brass tube-based contact terminals provided reliable electrical contacting for the PCEs
